- 2026-09-24: The national average peaked at about $4.48, the highest ever for that time of year. AAA's September 2026 news covers this period. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/2026/09/)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- 2026-09-04: about $4.15. 2026-09-24: about $4.48. 2026-10-01: $4.41. 2026-10-02: about $4.40. [chooseenergy](https://www.chooseenergy.com/data-center/cost-of-driving-by-state/), [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/national-average-dips-following-record-setting-september/)
- From September 24 to October 1 the average fell about 1 cent a day. Choose Energy's figure suggests about 1 cent more on October 2.
- On both sides of a crude move, the national average typically changes about 0 to 3 cents a day. Over 3 days that usually means a move of up to about ±5 to 8 cents. Pump prices react to crude with a delay of several days to two weeks, so the September 29 crude drop was probably still pushing prices down in early October.
- The seasonal switch to cheaper winter-blend gasoline (from September 15) usually pushes prices down in early October. I'm inferring this from general seasonal patterns, not a specific source.

The question is whether a $4.40 to $4.405 level stays at or above $4.38, which needs a drop of no more than about 2 to 2.5 cents. In this reference class that happens roughly 35 to 45% of the time.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- WTI rebounded $1.04 to $90.42 on September 30.
- Pump declines usually slow after the first sharp leg down.
- Prices are volatile because of the Middle East conflict.
- The October 2 level is still about 2 cents above the threshold.

Evidence for No:
- AAA showed $4.4137 on October 1 and about $4.40 on October 2, a fall of 1 to 1.3 cents a day.
- Pump prices were down about 7 cents in the week to October 1.
- The seasonal switch to winter-blend fuel keeps pushing prices down.
- Crude fell 3.5% on September 29, and that drop is still feeding through to pump prices with a lag.

(e) No scenario: the decline continues at about 1 cent a day over the weekend, and AAA shows $4.37 on October 5.
Yes scenario: the September 30 crude bounce and some Hormuz headlines slow the decline to under 1 cent a day, and the national average holds at about $4.385.

(f) I start from a 40% base rate. The extrapolated October 5 value sits right at or just under the threshold, and the slowing effect of the crude rebound roughly cancels out the winter-blend and lagged-crude pressure. So I keep the estimate near 40%.

Probability: 40%
